neighbours.label: a word marking the occupational/commercial sense, work as livelihood vs personal life (' business', ' job', ' profession', ' commercial')
fire: He bought the van second-hand and now uses it mostly for his plumbing business.
She learned most of what she knows about negotiation while on the job in sales.
The city charges higher parking fees for commercial vehicles than for private cars.
Teaching was never just a job for him; he saw it as a lifelong profession.
We keep the laptop for business and use the old tablet for everything else.
Bakers who sell bread as a business need a licence from the health department.
After ten years in the profession, she opened her own law office downtown.
The new rules apply only to commercial fishing boats, not to weekend anglers.
quiet: He bought the van second-hand and now uses it mostly for family camping trips.
She learned most of what she knows about negotiation while haggling at markets.
The city charges higher parking fees for visitors than for local residents.
Teaching his grandchildren to read was a joy that filled his retirement.
We keep the laptop for homework and use the old tablet for everything else.
Bakers who bake bread at home often start with a simple sourdough recipe.
After ten years in the city, she bought a small house near the river.
The new rules apply only to large boats, not to small rowing dinghies.

notes: card: peaks on ' business', ' job', ' commercial', ' profession(al)', ' religious' (vocation), often contrasted with personal use ('our personal trucks not the ones we had for our business'). Near misses keep the scene but use personal/private wording.
